evidence: "The reimplantation technique is preferred in adults due to the higher rate of re-intervention secondary to aortic regurgitation, observed in the remodelling technique." (PMID:39250726, P51)

papers.title: Extracellular Tuning of Mitochondrial Respiration Leads to Aortic Aneurysm.
papers.summary: The study identifies extracellular-matrix–regulated mitochondrial dysfunction in vascular smooth muscle cells as a driver of thoracic aortic aneurysm in Marfan syndrome, with reduced TFAM and mtDNA observed in mouse aortas and patient samples. The NAD+ precursor nicotinamide riboside restored mitochondrial respiration and reversed aortic dilation, blood pressure, and medial remodeling in Fbn1C1039G/+ mice, while improving mitochondrial and profibrotic readouts in human Marfan fibroblasts in vitro.
papers.why: Nicotinamide riboside rapidly reversed aortic aneurysms in a Marfan mouse model by restoring VSMC mitochondrial metabolism, supported by molecular and metabolic analyses in mice and patients.

papers.title: Perspectives on the revised Ghent criteria for the diagnosis of Marfan syndrome
papers.summary: This review concludes that Ghent-1 and revised Ghent (Ghent-2) criteria have similar diagnostic performance, but Ghent-2 is easier to use; neither has a diagnostic reference standard, so sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy cannot be established. Molecular confirmation of FBN1 mutations is emphasized to reduce diagnostic uncertainty and distinguish Marfan syndrome from related syndromes, while the review also describes cardiovascular therapies and mechanistic biomarkers relevant to aortic disease.
papers.why: Reviews and quantitatively compares the existing Ghent diagnostic criteria for Marfan syndrome and reports their diagnostic performance and practical utility.

papers.title: Irbesartan in Marfan syndrome (AIMS): a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial.
papers.summary: The AIMS double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial found that irbesartan reduced the annual rate of aortic root dilatation in children and adults with Marfan syndrome over approximately 5 years compared with placebo. The treatment was well tolerated, but the study was not powered to establish effects on clinical outcomes, and TGF-β concentrations did not differ between groups.
papers.why: A randomized, double-blind trial in 192 people with Marfan syndrome found that irbesartan reduced aortic-root dilatation compared with placebo.

papers.title: Aortopathy in a Mouse Model of Marfan Syndrome Is Not Mediated by Altered Transforming Growth Factor beta Signaling
papers.summary: In young Fbn1 C1039G/+ mice, ascending aortic dilation and medial elastin damage developed without detectable increases in aortic smooth-muscle-cell TGF-β signaling. SMC-specific deletion of Tgfbr2 reduced signaling and exacerbated aortopathy, indicating that physiological SMC TGF-β signaling is protective rather than pathogenic during early Marfan-associated aortopathy.
papers.why: This study develops and tests genetically modified Marfan mouse models that directly examine TGF-beta signaling's contribution to aortopathy.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies an Il1rn+/Trem1+ macrophage subpopulation as a cellular target for mitigating the progression of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection
papers.summary: This study identifies an Il1rn+/Trem1+ pro-inflammatory aortic macrophage subpopulation as a major source of inflammatory cytokines and MMPs during thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection (TAAD), including TAAD associated with Marfan syndrome. In BAPN-induced mouse TAAD, macrophage depletion with Ki20227 and TREM1 blockade with mLR12 reduced TAAD incidence, aortic rupture, or death, supporting transfer of this anti-inflammatory strategy to Marfan-associated TAAD.
papers.why: Identifies an Il1rn+/Trem1+ macrophage target and demonstrates that Ki20227 or TREM1 blockade reduces TAAD progression or rupture in mice, offering tools transferable to Marfan-associated aortic disease.

papers.title: Angiotensin receptor blockers and beta blockers in Marfan syndrome: an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials
papers.summary: An individual patient data meta-analysis of seven randomised trials found that angiotensin receptor blockers approximately halved the annual rate of aortic root enlargement in patients with Marfan syndrome who had not undergone prior aortic surgery, including among patients already receiving a β blocker. The benefit was particularly evident in patients with a pathogenic FBN1 variant; β blockers had a similar estimated effect, but the trials were underpowered to establish differences in aortic dissection, surgery, or death.
papers.why: This randomized-trial individual-patient meta-analysis directly compares ARBs and beta blockers in Marfan syndrome and establishes their effects on aortic-root growth.

papers.title: Long-term clinical outcomes of losartan in patients with Marfan syndrome: follow-up of the multicentre randomized controlled COMPARE trial.
papers.summary: In a long-term follow-up of the COMPARE trial, continuous losartan use, generally alongside β-blocker therapy, was associated with fewer deaths, aortic dissections, and a significant reduction in the composite clinical endpoint over approximately 8 years. The effect on elective aortic root replacement and reoperation was not statistically significant, and the authors note the retrospective design, patient crossover, limited event numbers, and need for further prospective evidence.
papers.why: Long-term follow-up from the COMPARE trial reports fewer deaths, dissections, and composite cardiovascular events among Marfan patients using losartan with regular treatment.

papers.title: Inflammation Aggravates Disease Severity in Marfan Syndrome Patients
papers.summary: The paper shows that increased TGF-β signaling and inflammation are associated with Marfan syndrome phenotype, with TGF-β marking aortic root dilatation and inflammatory markers such as M-CSF, HLA-DRB1, and HLA-DRB5 associated with disease severity or aortic progression. Existing anti-inflammatory or TGF-β-modulating approaches, particularly losartan, doxycycline, and anti-TGF-β antibodies, improved aortic phenotypes in cited mouse models, supporting their investigation as transferable strategies for human Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: Patient tissue and blood profiling identifies measurable inflammatory and TGF-beta biomarkers associated with aortic, ocular, and skeletal severity in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Efficacy and Mechanism of Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker Treatment in Experimental Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms
papers.summary: The paper shows that telmisartan and irbesartan suppress abdominal aortic aneurysm formation, progression, and mortality in two mouse models, whereas doxycycline, fluvastatin, and bosentan do not show meaningful benefit in the Ang II/ApoE−/− model. These findings concern abdominal rather than Marfan-associated thoracic aneurysms, and the authors state that ARB efficacy in human abdominal aortic aneurysm remains unproven and is being evaluated in a clinical trial.
papers.why: Telmisartan and irbesartan suppress aneurysm development in two mechanistically related mouse models and provide transferable evidence for aortic aneurysm research.

papers.title: Resveratrol Inhibits Aortic Root Dilatation in the Fbn1C1039G/+ Marfan Mouse Model
papers.summary: In the Fbn1C1039G/+ Marfan mouse model, resveratrol reduced aortic root dilatation more effectively than losartan while improving medial area, elastin integrity, and smooth-muscle-cell survival. Its benefit was independent of measurable SIRT1 activation, reduced senescence, TGF-β signaling, or leukocyte infiltration and involved endothelial-cell-dependent downregulation of miR-29b; SRT1720 and sirtinol did not significantly alter aortic root dilatation.
papers.why: The Marfan mouse study directly demonstrates that resveratrol inhibits aortic-root dilation through elastin preservation, smooth-muscle survival, and microRNA-29b downregulation.

papers.title: Marfan syndrome: current perspectives.
papers.summary: This review describes Marfan syndrome as an FBN1-associated connective-tissue disease with major cardiovascular complications and evaluates diagnostic, surgical, pharmacological, genetic, and biomarker approaches. It reports mixed clinical evidence for losartan, with apparent benefit in some FBN1 haploinsufficiency cases but no reduction of aortic dilation in a large randomized trial, while beta-receptor blockers remain first-line therapy and several biochemical and imaging biomarkers remain investigational.
papers.why: The review reports clinically evaluated Marfan therapies and candidate circulating biomarkers for disease severity and aortic-progression assessment.

papers.title: Aortic disease in Marfan syndrome is caused by overactivation of sGC-PRKG signaling by NO
papers.summary: The study identifies overactivation of the nitric oxide–soluble guanylate cyclase–cGMP-dependent protein kinase pathway as a causal mechanism of aortic disease in Marfan syndrome and shows elevated pathway activity in patients and Fbn1C1039G/+ mice. sGC inhibition, PRKG inhibition, and aortic Prkg1 silencing improved aortic phenotypes in mice, while plasma cGMP, protein nitration, and the nitrated plasma index emerged as candidate monitoring biomarkers that require further validation.
papers.why: The study identifies NO-sGC-PRKG overactivation as a causal Marfan mechanism and demonstrates reversal of aortopathy with pharmacological or gene-silencing interventions while nominating monitorable biomarkers.

papers.title: Gene panel sequencing in heritable thoracic aortic disorders and related entities - results of comprehensive testing in a cohort of 264 patients.
papers.summary: In 264 unrelated probands with heritable thoracic aortic disorders or related phenotypes, seven-gene next-generation sequencing identified a causal mutation in 13% overall and established Marfan syndrome diagnoses in patients with FBN1 variants despite nonclassic or overlapping clinical presentations. The study also found clinically significant SMAD3, TGFB2, and COL3A1 variants in patients meeting Marfan or revised Ghent criteria, supporting broad H-TAD panel testing after negative targeted FBN1 analysis while retaining MLPA for deletions and insertions that NGS may miss.
papers.why: The study validates an NGS assay including FBN1 and other thoracic-aortic genes, detecting clinically relevant variants in 13% of a 264-patient cohort that includes Marfan cases.

papers.title: Glycoproteomic Analysis of the Aortic Extracellular Matrix in Marfan Patients
papers.summary: The study identifies enhanced MFAP4 abundance and N-glycosylation in aneurysmal aortic extracellular matrix from patients with Marfan syndrome and shows that MFAP4 knockdown alters elastin, fibrillin-1, versican, and ADAMTS expression in aortic smooth muscle cells. High plasma MFAP4 was associated with reduced descending-aortic distensibility and increased type B aortic dissection risk, supporting it as a candidate risk biomarker that requires confirmation in larger cohorts.
papers.why: Direct Marfan aortic-tissue glycoproteomics identifies MFAP4 as a prognostic biomarker and uses targeted knockdown to probe its effects on FBN1 and elastin.

papers.title: Targeting feed-forward signaling of TGFbeta/NOX4/DHFR/eNOS uncoupling/TGFbeta axis with anti-TGFbeta and folic acid attenuates formation of aortic aneurysms: Novel mechanisms and therapeutics
papers.summary: In Fbn1C1039G/+ mice with Marfan syndrome, the study identifies a feed-forward TGFβ/NOX4/DHFR/eNOS-uncoupling pathway that promotes aortic aneurysm formation through reduced endothelial DHFR, H4B deficiency, oxidative stress, and impaired nitric oxide bioavailability. Anti-TGFβ and folic acid attenuate the pathway and largely prevent aortic dilation in mice, while circulating H4B is proposed as a biomarker of aneurysm size; these interventions were not tested in patients with Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: Intervention studies in a Marfan mouse model show that anti-TGF-beta therapy and folic acid prevent aortic aneurysm formation, while circulating tetrahydrobiopterin is supported as a predictive biomarker.

papers.title: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonists alleviate muscle pathology in the mouse model for laminin-α2-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy (MDC1A).
papers.summary: The paper identifies losartan/AT1 antagonism as a transferable approach for Marfan syndrome because AT1 inhibition suppresses profibrotic TGF-β signaling; cited mouse studies report reduced fibrosis and improved muscle architecture, function, and regeneration in Fbn1 mutant mice. In the paper's own severe MDC1A model, the losartan derivative L-158809 similarly suppressed AT1–TSP-1–TGF-β signaling, reduced fibrosis and inflammation, improved regeneration and function, but did not correct muscle-fiber size distribution or apoptosis.
papers.why: Treatment data in another genetic disease show that AT1 antagonism suppresses TGF-beta-driven fibrosis and improves muscle pathology through a pathway also implicated in Marfan aortopathy.

papers.title: Single-Cell Analysis of Aneurysmal Aortic Tissue in Patients with Marfan Syndrome Reveals Dysfunctional TGF-beta Signaling
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunostaining of aneurysmal ascending aortic tissue from three patients with Marfan syndrome identified increased proportions of de-differentiated, proliferative smooth muscle cells, reduced expression of mature contractile markers, and increased extracellular-matrix gene expression. Despite fibroblast-specific upregulation of TGFB1, receptors and downstream SMAD genes were broadly reduced, supporting impaired canonical TGF-β signaling in advanced MFS aortic disease.
papers.why: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling of Marfan aortic tissue provides a reusable method and mechanistic datasets identifying dysfunctional TGF-beta signaling and altered smooth-muscle differentiation.

papers.title: The importance of genotype-phenotype correlation in the clinical management of Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort shows that FBN-1 genetic testing and modified Ghent criteria diagnose Marfan syndrome, while variant type helps stratify aortic risk: truncating FBN-1 variants were associated with more aortic events than missense variants, although the age-at-event difference was not statistically significant. The paper also reports successful use of valve-sparing aortic root replacement and cites evidence that FBN-1 haploinsufficiency may respond better to losartan, but it does not directly test drug efficacy.
papers.why: Prospective data from FBN1-variant patients show that genotype can support diagnosis and predict aortic-event risk for clinical management.

papers.title: Androgens Accentuate TGF-β Dependent Erk/Smad Activation During Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Formation in Marfan Syndrome Male Mice.
papers.summary: In the Fbn1 C1039G/+ mouse model of Marfan syndrome, male mice showed greater thoracic aortic aneurysm growth than females, accompanied by increased androgen-associated TGF-β–dependent Erk1/2 and Smad2 activation and MMP-2 activity. Dihydrotestosterone potentiated these molecular and extracellular-matrix-remodeling responses in aortic smooth muscle cells, whereas androgen blockade with flutamide reduced aneurysm growth, elastin breakdown, signaling, and MMP-2 activity in male mice.
papers.why: In Marfan mice, flutamide reduces aneurysm growth and ERK/Smad signaling, with complementary smooth-muscle-cell experiments supporting the mechanism.

papers.title: Transforming Growth Factor-beta and the Renin-Angiotensin System in Syndromic Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: Implications for Treatment
papers.summary: This review concludes that excessive TGF-β signaling, renin-angiotensin system activation, impaired aortic vascular smooth muscle cell mechanosensing, extracellular-matrix degradation, and fibrosis jointly drive syndromic thoracic aortic aneurysm pathology in Marfan syndrome. Preclinical approaches targeting TGF-β, AT1R, ERK1/2, or MMPs can attenuate aortic disease, but clinical results for ARBs and β-blockers are heterogeneous, with mutation-dependent efficacy and insufficient evidence for major clinical outcomes.
papers.why: The review evaluates clinical trial evidence for ARBs and beta-blockers as disease-modifying strategies for syndromic thoracic aortic aneurysm, including Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Optimising the mutation screening strategy in Marfan syndrome and identifying genotypes with more severe aortic involvement.
papers.summary: In 136 patients with Marfan syndrome or Marfanoid habitus, sequencing followed by a nine-gene panel and FBN1 multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification achieved an overall mutation-detection rate of 62%. FBN1 variants eliminating a disulphide-bonding cysteine were associated with greater aortic involvement, more frequent aortic surgery, and more frequent ectopia lentis, while Loeys-Dietz syndrome could present with low systemic scores but severe aortic disease.
papers.why: The study establishes a high-yield Marfan diagnostic testing strategy and identifies FBN1 mutation classes associated with increased aortic involvement.

papers.title: The role of the multidisciplinary health care team in the management of patients with Marfan syndrome
papers.summary: This review describes a multidisciplinary care model for Marfan syndrome centered on coordinated surveillance, genetic and imaging-based diagnosis, cardiovascular risk management, prophylactic surgery, and patient-centered support. It reports favorable experience with Marfan centers and selected center-specific observations, while emphasizing that some MFS rehabilitation programs and specialized diagnostic approaches lack scientific evaluation.
papers.why: The paper describes an established multidisciplinary care infrastructure and coordinated management program specifically for patients with Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Mitral annulus disjunction is associated with adverse outcome in Marfan and Loeys-Dietz syndromes
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 103 patients with Marfan syndrome and 65 with Loeys–Dietz syndrome, echocardiographic mitral annulus disjunction was common and identified a severe phenotype characterized by aortic events at younger age and greater need for mitral valve surgery. MAD was associated with mitral valve prolapse, mitral regurgitation, and larger mitral annuli, while aortic events and ventricular arrhythmias occurred with and without MAD and adjustment did not establish an independent association with several ventricular or diastolic measures.
papers.why: This study identifies mitral annulus disjunction as an echocardiographic marker associated with earlier aortic events and mitral valve surgery in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Generation of heterozygous fibrillin-1 mutant cloned pigs from genome-edited foetal fibroblasts.
papers.summary: The study generated cloned pigs carrying a heterozygous porcine FBN1 mutation that reproduced selected Marfan syndrome phenotypes, including skeletal abnormalities and disrupted elastic fibers in the proximal thoracic aorta, although some human manifestations were absent. It also found variable expressivity among genetically similar clones and more severe, often lethal disease in homozygous offspring, supporting use of these pigs to study FBN1 pathogenesis and epigenetic modifiers of Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: The study generates a genetically engineered pig model with FBN1 mutation and human-like Marfan phenotypes suitable for pathogenesis studies and treatment development.

papers.title: The revised role of TGF-beta in aortic aneurysms in Marfan syndrome
papers.summary: In this COMPARE trial sub-study, losartan did not uniformly lower plasma TGF-β in adults with Marfan syndrome, and patients whose TGF-β decreased had higher baseline TGF-β and higher subsequent aortic root dilatation rates. The authors propose that TGF-β is primarily a readout of aortic disease, whereas angiotensin II–AT1 signaling may initiate vascular pathology and mediate losartan’s protective effect.
papers.why: Longitudinal patient data showed that changes in plasma TGF-beta after losartan were associated with differing three-year aortic-root dilation rates.

papers.title: Design and rationale of a prospective, collaborative meta-analysis of all randomized controlled trials of angiotensin receptor antagonists in Marfan syndrome, based on individual patient data: A report from the Marfan Treatment Trialists' Collaboration
papers.summary: This paper presents the rationale and statistical analysis plan for a prospective individual-patient-data meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating angiotensin receptor antagonists (ARBs) and beta-blockers in Marfan syndrome. It does not report new treatment results; the evidence discussed indicates that losartan reduced aortic dilation in two small randomized Marfan trials and rescued the aortic phenotype in a mouse model through down-regulation of TGF-beta signaling, while the planned meta-analysis will address the limited precision of individual trials.
papers.why: Defines a prospective collaborative method for evaluating ARBs and beta-blockade across approximately 2,300 Marfan trial participants using standardized subgroup and clinical endpoints.

papers.title: Fibrillin-1 regulates endothelial sprouting during angiogenesis.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The study shows that mutant fibrillin-1 in Fbn1C1041G/+ mice impairs retinal angiogenesis by disrupting endothelial tip/stalk cell specification and VEGF/Notch–Smad signaling. Intravitreal recombinant C-terminal fibrillin-1 restored retinal vascular growth, tip-cell markers, MAGP1 deposition, and ADAMTS1 expression, while also promoting endothelial sprouting in vitro.
papers.why: A recombinant fibrillin-1 fragment directly rescued angiogenic and signaling defects in a Marfan mouse model, while the mouse retina and cell-culture systems provide reusable experimental platforms.

papers.title: Anatomically specific reactive oxygen species production participates in Marfan syndrome aneurysm formation.
papers.summary: In the Fbn1C1039G/+ mouse model of Marfan syndrome, reactive oxygen species and NADPH oxidase activity are elevated specifically in aneurysmal ascending aorta, and AngII increases the activity in a TGF-β-dependent manner. The nonspecific NADPH oxidase inhibitor apocynin attenuates—but does not prevent—aneurysm growth while reducing ROS production, elastin fragmentation, protease activity, and extracellular-matrix destruction.
papers.why: In a Marfan mouse model, apocynin reduced aortic aneurysm formation, elastin fragmentation, and protease activity, while anatomically resolved assays identified a potentially targetable TGF-β-dependent NADPH oxidase/ROS pathway.

papers.title: In vivo characterization of doxycycline-mediated protection of aortic function and structure in a mouse model of Marfan syndrome-associated aortic aneurysm.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal mouse study, long-term sub-antimicrobial doxycycline reduced aortic-root growth, left-ventricular mass, pulse-wave velocity, MMP-2/MMP-9 expression, and elastic-fiber fragmentation associated with Marfan syndrome. These findings provide preclinical evidence of protection against MFS-associated aortic aneurysm, but the treatment was not tested in patients and did not completely prevent age-related aortic stiffness or reverse all elastic-fiber abnormalities.
papers.why: Long-term doxycycline reduced aortic root growth and improved vascular elasticity and elastic-fiber organization in a Marfan mouse model.

papers.title: Deregulated microRNA and mRNA expression profiles in the peripheral blood of patients with Marfan syndrome
papers.summary: Peripheral-blood microarray profiling followed by independent RT-qPCR validation identified 11 miRNAs and 6 mRNAs differentially expressed in Marfan syndrome, with enrichment of apoptosis, JAK/STAT, integrin-signaling, and angiogenesis pathways. Several validated transcripts correlated with aortic root Z-score, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, age, or mitral valve prolapse, supporting their candidacy—rather than established clinical utility—as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
papers.why: The study provides patient blood expression data and identifies candidate diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic biomarkers in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Structural equation modeling of the quality of life for patients with marfan syndrome
papers.summary: This study found that social support, disease-related factors, and biobehavioral factors explained 72.4% of quality of life in 218 adults with Marfan syndrome, with biobehavioral factors having the strongest direct association. Anxiety, depression, fatigue, pain, body image, aortic disease, cardiovascular surgery burden, and social support are therefore presented as clinically relevant targets for quality-of-life assessment and potential intervention development.
papers.why: The 218-patient analysis provides a disease-specific quality-of-life model identifying modifiable biobehavioral, social, and disease factors for intervention studies.

papers.title: Genetic testing of 248 Chinese aortopathy patients using a panel assay.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 248 Chinese probands with aortic disease or suspected Marfan syndrome, a 15-gene next-generation sequencing panel identified likely pathogenic variants in 37.1% of participants, predominantly involving FBN1. FBN1 truncating or splicing mutations were associated with more severe aortic or valvular disease, while the iAorta pipeline and Sanger confirmation improved variant detection and reduced false-positive calls.
papers.why: The validated targeted panel and optimized analysis pipeline diagnosed inherited aortopathy in a large cohort that included patients with Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: The Effect of a Nonpeptide Angiotensin II Type 2 Receptor Agonist, Compound 21, on Aortic Aneurysm Growth in a Mouse Model of Marfan Syndrome.
papers.summary: In male Fbn1C1039G/+ mice modeling Marfan syndrome, losartan reduced aortic root growth, whereas the selective nonpeptide AT2 receptor agonist Compound 21 did not reduce aneurysm growth at the tested doses, including when treatment began at 10 days of age or when combined with renin–angiotensin system blockers. No treatment significantly improved the quantified aortic wall histology, although losartan-treated mice showed relatively preserved elastic fiber architecture.
papers.why: This intervention study tests established drugs and a new AT2 receptor agonist in an Fbn1-mutant Marfan mouse model, confirming losartan's reduction of aneurysm growth while finding Compound 21 ineffective.

papers.title: No Beneficial Effect of General and Specific Anti-Inflammatory Therapies on Aortic Dilatation in Marfan Mice
papers.summary: In adult FBN1 C1039G/+ Marfan mice with established aortic root dilatation, losartan reduced vascular inflammation, pSmad2 signaling, and aortic root enlargement over eight weeks. Methylprednisolone and abatacept reduced macrophage influx but did not prevent dilatation; methylprednisolone also increased alcian-blue-positive aortic damage, indicating that broad suppression of inflammation is not beneficial in this model.
papers.why: Controlled treatment experiments in a Marfan model show that losartan reduces aortic dilation whereas methylprednisolone and abatacept do not, identifying effective and ineffective interventions.

papers.title: Molecular characterization and investigation of the role of genetic variation in phenotypic variability and response to treatment in a large pediatric Marfan syndrome cohort
papers.summary: In a 373-patient pediatric Marfan syndrome cohort, molecular testing identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic FBN1 variant in 91% of patients and revealed strong genotype–phenotype associations, particularly for ectopia lentis and aortic root severity. FBN1 variant type or location did not significantly modify the three-year aortic root treatment response to losartan or atenolol.
papers.why: Testing of 373 severe pediatric Marfan cases established high FBN1 diagnostic yield and variant-specific associations with cardiovascular and ocular phenotypes.

papers.title: Characterization of large genomic deletions in the FBN1 gene using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification
papers.summary: In 14 patients with aortopathy and negative FBN1, TGFβR1, and TGFβR2 sequencing, multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification identified two previously unreported large FBN1 deletions in four patients with clinically diagnosed Marfan syndrome. The findings support FBN1 haploinsufficiency as a cause of Marfan syndrome and show that copy-number testing can identify pathogenic deletions missed by sequencing, while negative results do not exclude variants outside the tested regions.
papers.why: The study validates MLPA plus array analysis for detecting large FBN1 deletions and duplications in Marfan syndrome patients missed by sequencing.

papers.title: Versican accumulation drives Nos2 induction and aortic disease in Marfan syndrome via Akt activation.
papers.summary: This study identifies accumulated versican as a causal mediator of Marfan syndrome aortopathy in Fbn1C1041G/+ mice: Vcan silencing or haploinsufficiency reduces NOS2 expression, aortic dilation, and medial degeneration. Pharmacological mTOR/Akt inhibition with AZD8055 rapidly regressed aortic dilation and lowered NOS2, while human Marfan aortas showed VCAN accumulation and elevated AKT-S473 phosphorylation.
papers.why: The study demonstrates in Marfan mice that reducing versican or inhibiting Akt reverses aortic disease and supports VCAN and phospho-AKT as human disease biomarkers.

papers.title: Management of aortic disease in children with FBN1-related Marfan syndrome
papers.summary: This consensus review provides pediatric management recommendations for aortic disease in FBN1-related Marfan syndrome, emphasizing annual 2D-TTE surveillance, MRI or CTA when needed, beta-blocker or angiotensin-receptor-blocker therapy, and prophylactic valve-sparing aortic root surgery at defined risk thresholds. It also highlights limited evidence for some medical outcomes, the absence of reliable biomarkers for aortic events, and insufficient pediatric validation of PEARS and exercise recommendations.
papers.why: This consensus document provides actionable pediatric management strategies for aortic monitoring, treatment, surgery, and physical activity in FBN1-related Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: AP-1 Oligodeoxynucleotides Reduce Aortic Elastolysis in a Murine Model of Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: In cultured murine and human aortic smooth muscle cells, AP-1-neutralizing decoy oligodeoxynucleotides reduced MMP-2/MMP-9 expression and activity, smooth-muscle-cell migration, and reactive oxygen species formation. Ex vivo treatment of aortic grafts reduced medial elastolysis, MMP activity, and macrophage infiltration 30 days after implantation in the mgR/mgR Marfan mouse model, while no delivery aid was required for cellular uptake.
papers.why: The study tests AP-1 dODNs in Marfan mouse aortic smooth-muscle cells and grafted aortas, showing reduced MMP activity, elastolysis, macrophage infiltration, and vascular pathology.

papers.title: Interpretation and classification of FBN1 variants associated with Marfan syndrome: consensus recommendations from the Clinical Genome Resource's FBN1 variant curation expert panel.
papers.summary: The ClinGen FBN1 Variant Curation Expert Panel developed gene-specific adaptations to the ACMG/AMP criteria for classifying FBN1 variants associated with Marfan syndrome. In a 60-variant pilot study, these recommendations reduced uncertain classifications from 24 to 12, increased likely pathogenic classifications from 13 to 22, and yielded 85.0% concordance among participating institutions.
papers.why: The consensus panel supplies disease-specific rules, functional-assay guidance, and curated classifications for standardized FBN1 variant interpretation in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Dissecting aortic aneurysm in Marfan syndrome is associated with losartan-sensitive transcriptomic modulation of aortic cells.
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified an intimal, MFS-modulated aortic cell population in Fbn1mgR/mgR mice that is associated with dissecting thoracic aortic aneurysm and is transcriptomically similar to modulated SMC populations in mouse and human aneurysmal aorta. Chronic losartan treatment mitigated aneurysm progression and eliminated the MFSmod population, while computational analysis did not support enhanced canonical TGF-β signaling as its upstream driver.
papers.why: Single-cell profiling identified disease-specific aortic cell states in Marfan mice that were eliminated by losartan, linking a discrete cell population to treatment response and dissection risk.

papers.title: A new novel mutation in FBN1 causes autosomal dominant Marfan syndrome in a Chinese family
papers.summary: The study identified the heterozygous FBN1 c.640A>G (p.G214S) missense variant in all 13 affected members of a four-generation Chinese family with Marfan syndrome, but not in unaffected relatives or 100 controls. The findings support the variant's causal role and indicate that direct FBN1 sequencing can support diagnosis of Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: The study identifies a pathogenic heterozygous FBN1 G214S variant in a large Marfan family and demonstrates the diagnostic utility of direct FBN1 sequencing.

papers.title: Celiprolol
papers.summary: This review reports that celiprolol reduced arterial events threefold versus no treatment in a randomized trial of patients with vascular Ehlers–Danlos syndrome, with the clearest benefit in the COL3A1-mutant subgroup. It proposes celiprolol as a possible therapy for Marfan syndrome on mechanistic grounds, based on shared TGFβ-pathway involvement, but the paper provides no Marfan syndrome clinical data.
papers.why: Celiprolol was tested in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and significantly reduced arterial events, supporting transfer to Marfan-related arterial fragility on the basis of the shared connective-tissue and aortic phenotype.

papers.title: NGS analysis in Marfan syndrome spectrum: Combination of rare and common genetic variants to improve genotype-phenotype correlation analysis
papers.summary: In a cohort of 181 patients with a Marfan-like phenotype, an 11-gene NGS analysis combined rare and common variants to improve genotype–phenotype correlation and phenotypic classification. A phenotypic factor predicted pathogenic variants in FBN1, TGFBR1, or TGFBR2, while combined polygenic scores and rare-variant burden explained significantly more phenotypic variance than an FBN1-only model.
papers.why: The study validates an NGS analysis strategy in 181 Marfan-spectrum patients that improves phenotype classification and genotype-phenotype correlation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based analysis of body composition in Marfan: skeletal muscle density and psoas muscle index predict aortic enlargement
papers.summary: This retrospective study shows that AI-based analysis of L3 body composition is feasible from routine CT angiography in patients with Marfan syndrome. Higher skeletal muscle density and psoas muscle index were associated with progressive aortic enlargement and were significant predictors in multivariable logistic regression, although the cohort was small and retrospective.
papers.why: Automated CT body-composition analysis produced measurable muscle indicators that predicted progressive aortic enlargement in patients with Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Marfan Syndrome Caused by Disruption of the FBN1 Gene due to A Reciprocal Chromosome Translocation
papers.summary: In a mother and daughter with clinical Marfan syndrome, routine FBN1 sequence and copy-number testing was unrevealing, but cytogenetic and molecular analyses identified a reciprocal chromosome 2–15 translocation that disrupts FBN1 in intron 55. The study identifies optical genome mapping, supported by FISH, long-range PCR, and Nanopore sequencing, as a diagnostic approach for balanced structural variants causing FBN1-related Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: Optical genome mapping and breakpoint-resolving methods diagnosed an FBN1-disrupting balanced translocation missed by routine NGS in two Marfan patients.

papers.title: Identification of gross deletions in FBN1 gene by MLPA.
papers.summary: The study identified five previously unreported large FBN1 deletions in patients with suspected Marfan syndrome whose 15-gene sequencing panel results were negative, and four deletions were breakpoint-confirmed. The findings support adding FBN1 deletion/duplication testing by MLPA to the diagnostic evaluation of clinically suspected Marfan syndrome, while no gross TGFBR2 rearrangements were detected in this cohort.
papers.why: MLPA testing was validated in a Marfan and aneurysm cohort as a method for detecting large FBN1 deletions or duplications missed by routine sequencing.

papers.title: Therapeutic CCR2 Blockade Prevents Inflammation and Alleviates Myxomatous Valve Disease in Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: In the Fbn1C1039G/+ mouse model of Marfan syndrome, CCR2-positive immune-cell infiltration drives mitral-valve inflammation, inflammatory protease expression, pathological extracellular-matrix remodeling, and myxomatous valve degeneration. Genetic or pharmacological CCR2 inhibition, particularly with RS504393, prevented early disease, improved established disease, and restored valve morphology, but efficacy in human Marfan syndrome remains untested.
papers.why: Pharmacological CCR2 blockade prevented and slowed myxomatous valve disease in a Marfan mouse model while preserving valve extracellular-matrix integrity.

papers.title: Long-term miR-29b suppression reduces aneurysm formation in a Marfan mouse model.
papers.summary: In the Fbn1 C1039G/+ Marfan mouse model, systemic inhibition of miR-29b reduced the rate of ascending-aortic aneurysm formation, particularly when administered prenatally, by improving early elastogenesis, limiting matrix metalloproteinase activity, and preserving elastin. The treatment did not slow established aneurysm growth, aneurysms eventually still developed, and the study did not establish clinical efficacy in patients.
papers.why: Systemic miR-29b suppression substantially delayed aortic aneurysm development and improved elastin and matrix remodeling in a Marfan mouse model.

papers.title: Pleiotropic activation of endothelial function by angiotensin II receptor blockers is crucial to their protective anti-vascular remodeling effects
papers.summary: In mice, telmisartan activated eNOS-derived nitric oxide signaling and reduced aortic contractility independently of classic angiotensin II/AT1R signaling and, in the MFS model, prevented aortic root widening and pathological wall remodeling. NOS inhibition or eNOS deletion attenuated these protective effects, indicating that nitric oxide rather than blood-pressure lowering mediated the telmisartan response.
papers.why: The study directly reports telmisartan preventing Marfan-associated aortic root widening and correcting aberrant TGF-β signaling in a mouse model.

unread.title: Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: This Marfan-focused review identifies established diagnostic, imaging, medical, and surgical approaches for managing aortic disease and other major manifestations.

unread.title: The revised Ghent nosology for the Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: This paper presents a validated disease-specific diagnostic framework and scoring system for Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: What's new about angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) therapy for Marfan syndrome: A narrative review.
unread.why: The review reports pediatric aortic-root effects of losartan and experimental vascular effects of its active metabolites, directly supporting ARB strategies for Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Clinically relevant variants in a large cohort of Indian patients with Marfan syndrome and related disorders identified by next-generation sequencing
unread.why: The study demonstrates a 85% molecular diagnostic yield in a clinically suspected Marfan or related-disorder cohort using targeted next-generation sequencing.

unread.title: Effect of mutation type and location on clinical outcome in 1,013 probands with Marfan syndrome or related phenotypes and FBN1 mutations: an international study.
unread.why: This large multicenter study provides mutation-based prognostic stratification and clinical outcome data for more than 1,000 FBN1-positive probands.

unread.title: New population-based exome data question the pathogenicity of some genetic variants previously associated with Marfan syndrome
unread.why: The study evaluates a reusable computational and population-frequency workflow for identifying and reclassifying potentially false-positive FBN1 variants attributed to Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Endothelial Cell Senescence in Marfan Syndrome: Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Potential of TGF-beta Pathway Inhibition
unread.why: The study develops a patient-specific Marfan endothelial-cell model and shows that SB-431542 ameliorates senescence and functional dysfunction.

unread.title: Identification and in silico analyses of novel TGFBR1 and TGFBR2 mutations in Marfan syndrome-related disorders.
unread.why: This study develops and evaluates a genetic testing and in-silico variant-interpretation workflow for FBN1-negative Marfan-related disorders.

unread.title: Variants in ADRB1 and CYP2C9: Association with Response to Atenolol and Losartan in Marfan Syndrome.
unread.why: Trial-based pharmacogenetic analysis identifies an ADRB1 genotype associated with differential atenolol versus losartan response in Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Losartan, an AT1 antagonist, prevents aortic aneurysm in a mouse model of Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The Marfan mouse model directly demonstrates prevention of aortic aneurysm and partial reversal of pulmonary abnormalities by losartan or TGF-beta blockade.

unread.title: Angiotensin II blockade and aortic-root dilation in Marfan's syndrome.
unread.why: This small clinical cohort provides direct evidence that angiotensin II receptor blockade slows progressive aortic-root dilation in pediatric Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: TGFBR1 and TGFBR2 mutations in patients with features of Marfan syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome.
unread.why: Mutation screening in 41 patients demonstrates that TGFBR1 or TGFBR2 testing identifies Marfan-like phenotypes missed by FBN1 testing.

unread.title: Two novel and one known mutation of the TGFBR2 gene in Marfan syndrome not associated with FBN1 gene defects.
unread.why: This study directly supports TGFBR2 genetic testing as a diagnostic solution for FBN1-negative patients with Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Prevalence of dural ectasia in 63 gene-mutation-positive patients with features of Marfan syndrome type 1 and Loeys-Dietz syndrome and report of 22 novel FBN1 mutations.
unread.why: The study assessed dural ectasia in mutation-positive Marfan and Loeys-Dietz patients and quantified its prevalence as a clinically measurable Marfan criterion.

unread.title: High-Throughput Genomics Identify Novel FBN1/2 Variants in Severe Neonatal Marfan Syndrome and Congenital Heart Defects
unread.why: The report demonstrates use of WES and genome-wide SNP microarray analysis to identify FBN1/FBN2 variants and characterize severe neonatal Marfan phenotypes with congenital heart defects.

unread.title: Analysis of FBN1, TGFβ2, TGFβR1 and TGFβR2 mRNA as Key Molecular Mechanisms in the Damage of Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection in Marfan Syndrome.
unread.why: RT-qPCR in Marfan aortic surgical tissue identified disease- and dissection-associated expression changes in FBN1 and TGF-beta pathway genes, supporting candidate molecular biomarkers.

unread.title: Targeted next-generation sequencing reveals the genetic mechanism of Chinese Marfan syndrome cohort with ocular manifestation
unread.why: A targeted NGS cohort of 318 participants demonstrated high diagnostic yield for FBN1 and identified potentially relevant ocular-phenotype variants in other Marfan-related genes.

unread.title: Single-Cell Proteomics Uncovers Cell-Specific Proteins in Vascular Health and Marfan Syndrome Disease-Brief Report.
unread.why: Single-cell proteomics generated a human and mouse Marfan aortic atlas and identified cell-state-specific proteins, including matrix effectors and regulators of fibrillin-1 abundance.

unread.title: Detection of six novel FBN1 mutations in British patients affected by Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The study provides direct evidence that single-strand conformation analysis is a reliable, cost-effective FBN1 screening method with an 80% mutation yield in the tested cohort.

unread.title: Single-Nucleus Multiomic Analyses Identifies Gene Regulatory Dynamics of Phenotypic Modulation in Human Aneurysmal Aortic Root.
unread.why: The study provides human MFS aortic-root single-nucleus multiomic and spatial transcriptomic methods and experimentally identifies FOXN3 as a regulator of the VSMC contractile phenotype.

unread.title: Assembly assay identifies a critical region of human fibrillin-1 required for 10-12 nm diameter microfibril biogenesis
unread.why: The study develops and applies a fibrillin-1 microfibril assembly assay to compare MFS variants and identify distinct assembly-disrupting mechanisms.

unread.title: Classification and Interpretation for 11 FBN1 Variants Responsible for Marfan Syndrome and Pre-implantation Genetic Testing (PGT) for Two Families Successfully Blocked Transmission of the Pathogenic Mutations
unread.why: The study reports FBN1 diagnostic interpretation and successfully applied preimplantation genetic testing with haplotype analysis to prevent transmission in two MFS families.

unread.title: Novel pharmacological strategies to prevent aortic complications in Marfan syndrome
unread.why: The review summarizes evidence that losartan and other pharmacological strategies prevent or reduce aortic disease in MFS models and a small pediatric cohort.

unread.title: Three FBN1 pathogenic variants in Chinese patients with Marfan syndrome: Two novel variants including a splicing-altering deletion with functional verification.
unread.why: The study combines clinical sequencing, bioinformatics interpretation, and functional minigene verification to diagnose and characterize novel FBN1 variants in MFS.

unread.title: Introducing Allopurinol to the Medical Treatment of Marfan Syndrome: Advantages, Limitations, and Potential Extension to other Aortopathies.
unread.why: The review identifies allopurinol as a concrete MFS drug candidate supported by preclinical MFS mouse data and reports its orphan-drug designation.

unread.title: IL11 (Interleukin-11) Causes Emphysematous Lung Disease in a Mouse Model of Marfan Syndrome
unread.why: The study demonstrates in genetic and pharmacologic MFS mouse models that IL11 signaling drives pulmonary disease and that IL11 or IL11RA inhibition protects lung and aortic pathology.

unread.title: Phenotype-driven clustering of ocular manifestations reveals prognostic and genetic heterogeneity in Marfan syndrome: a real-world longitudinal cohort study
unread.why: The study validates ocular biomarkers, prognostic outcomes, and an unsupervised subtype-classification tool in a large FBN1-positive Marfan cohort.

unread.title: Blocking Compensatory Matrix Cross-Linking Accelerates Thoracic Aortopathy in a Mouse Model of Marfan Syndrome
unread.why: The Marfan mouse experiment directly tests a therapeutically actionable extracellular-matrix target and provides evidence that augmenting rather than suppressing protective collagen cross-linking may reduce aortopathy.

unread.title: Imaging-Based Age- and Sex-Related Cardiovascular and Skeletal Phenotypes in Fbn1 C1041G/+ Mice
unread.why: This study establishes age- and sex-resolved cardiovascular, valvular, and skeletal endpoints for preclinical testing in a Fbn1 Marfan mouse model.

unread.title: MMP-2 regulates Erk1/2 phosphorylation and aortic dilatation in Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: Direct data from Marfan mice show that MMP-2 inhibition with doxycycline suppresses aortic disease, while losartan-doxycycline combination therapy normalizes aortic structure and markedly improves survival.

unread.title: Update on Clinical Trials of Losartan With and Without β-Blockers to Block Aneurysm Growth in Patients With Marfan Syndrome: A Review.
unread.why: The review synthesizes clinical trial evidence directly relevant to selecting beta-blocker or angiotensin-receptor-blocker therapy and highlights the need for adequately powered hard-outcome trials in Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Effectiveness of combination of losartan potassium and doxycycline versus single-drug treatments in the secondary prevention of thoracic aortic aneurysm in Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The combination of losartan and doxycycline completely prevented established thoracic aneurysm development and restored vascular function in a Marfan mouse model, exceeding either monotherapy.

unread.title: Atenolol versus losartan in children and young adults with Marfan's syndrome.
unread.why: A large randomized trial provides direct comparative evidence that losartan and atenolol have similar effects on aortic-root growth in children and young adults with Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Tgfbr2 disruption in postnatal smooth muscle impairs aortic wall homeostasis.
unread.why: Rapamycin prevented dissection caused by smooth-muscle Tgfbr2 disruption and protected against aneurysm growth in a Marfan mouse model, revealing a transferable pathway-level treatment approach.

unread.title: Circulating transforming growth factor-beta in Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The study validates circulating total TGF-beta1 as a pharmacodynamic and potential prognostic biomarker that is elevated in Marfan syndrome and decreases with losartan or beta-blocker therapy.

unread.title: Therapies for Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms and Acute Aortic Dissections.
unread.why: This disease-focused review consolidates tested and emerging interventions for Marfan-associated thoracic aortic disease, including pharmacologic treatment, imaging, surgery, and model-based mechanistic testing.

unread.title: Identification of the minimal combination of clinical features in probands for efficient mutation detection in the FBN1 gene.
unread.why: Analysis of 586 probands establishes a clinical screening rule that efficiently identifies patients most likely to harbor pathogenic FBN1 variants and optimizes molecular testing resources.

unread.title: Echocardiographic methods, quality review, and measurement accuracy in a randomized multicenter clinical trial of Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The study validates a standardized, highly reproducible echocardiographic assay and outcome measure for tracking aortic-root growth in multicenter Marfan trials.

unread.title: The effect of losartan on progressive aortic dilatation in patients with Marfan's syndrome: a meta-analysis of prospective randomized clinical trials.
unread.why: A meta-analysis of six randomized trials in Marfan syndrome reports that losartan reduces progressive aortic dilatation and evaluates clinically relevant aortic outcomes.

unread.title: Identification of novel FBN1 and TGFBR2 mutations in 65 probands with Marfan syndrome or Marfan-like phenotypes.
unread.why: The study reports mutation-detection and variant-classification methods with data from 65 probands having Marfan syndrome or Marfan-like phenotypes.

unread.title: PIEZO1 attenuates Marfan syndrome aneurysm development through TGF-β signaling pathway inhibition via TGFBR2.
unread.why: The study identifies Yoda1 activation of PIEZO1 as a treatment that reverses thoracic aortic aneurysm phenotypes in a Marfan mouse model through TGFBR2 endocytosis and autophagy.

unread.title: Next-generation sequencing identifies novel mutations in the FBN1 gene for two Chinese families with Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The paper reports a rapid targeted-sequencing method that identified pathogenic FBN1 mutations in two unrelated Marfan syndrome families.

unread.title: Aggressive approach for spontaneous pneumothorax treatment in children with Marfan syndrome?
unread.why: A pediatric cohort including nine Marfan patients provides management data showing higher pneumothorax recurrence and treatment failure and supporting more aggressive initial care.

unread.title: Revised diagnostic criteria for the Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The paper directly provides revised, clinically usable diagnostic criteria incorporating skeletal findings and molecular testing for Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor blockade attenuates TGF-beta-induced failure of muscle regeneration in multiple myopathic states.
unread.why: The study demonstrates in a Marfan mouse model that losartan and direct TGF-beta neutralization rescue defective muscle regeneration and function.

unread.title: Evidence for a critical contribution of haploinsufficiency in the complex pathogenesis of Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The paper develops Marfan-relevant mouse models and demonstrates that restoring wild-type FBN1 rescues the aortic phenotype in a haploinsufficient model.

unread.title: Recommendations for physical activity and recreational sports participation for young patients with genetic cardiovascular diseases.
unread.why: This guideline provides an existing clinical framework for prescribing and restricting physical activity in young people with Marfan and other inherited cardiovascular diseases.

unread.title: Losartan reduces aortic dilatation rate in adults with Marfan syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
unread.why: This randomized trial directly shows that losartan slows aortic root dilatation in adults with Marfan syndrome and defines imaging-based efficacy endpoints.

unread.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society position statement on the management of thoracic aortic disease.
unread.why: This clinical practice guideline provides directly reusable surgical thresholds, surveillance strategies, risk-assessment methods, and management recommendations for the thoracic aortic disease that drives Marfan morbidity.

unread.title: Beneficial Outcome of Losartan Therapy Depends on Type of FBN1 Mutation in Marfan Syndrome.
unread.why: A randomized three-year substudy shows that losartan reduces aortic-root dilation specifically in patients with FBN1 haploinsufficiency and establishes a genotype-stratified response measure.

unread.title: Identification of 23 TGFBR2 and 6 TGFBR1 gene mutations and genotype-phenotype investigations in 457 patients with Marfan syndrome type I and II, Loeys-Dietz syndrome and related disorders.
unread.why: Screening 457 patients yields actionable diagnostic mutation-detection rates and distinguishes classical Marfan from TGFBR1/2-related connective-tissue disease.

unread.title: Inhibition of Marfan Syndrome Aortic Root Dilation by Losartan: Role of Angiotensin II Receptor Type 1-Independent Activation of Endothelial Function.
unread.why: Multiple transgenic and pharmacologic models show that losartan and endothelial NOS activation can block Marfan aortic-root dilation independently of blood-pressure lowering or ATR1 inhibition.

unread.title: Comprehensive genetic analysis of relevant four genes in 49 patients with Marfan syndrome or Marfan-related phenotypes.
unread.why: Direct sequencing of 49 Marfan or suspected-Marfan patients provides a validated diagnostic strategy, detection rates, and identification of TGFBR-related phenocopies.

unread.title: Evaluating the quality of Marfan genotype-phenotype correlations in existing FBN1 databases.
unread.why: The paper evaluates major FBN1 variant resources and introduces a Marfan score and curated genotype-phenotype database for variant interpretation.

unread.title: Muscle and Bone Impairment in Children With Marfan Syndrome: Correlation With Age and FBN1 Genotype.
unread.why: The study quantifies age- and genotype-associated bone and muscle deficits in Marfan syndrome and supports longitudinal DXA and vitamin D monitoring.

unread.title: Elevated expression levels of lysyl oxidases protect against aortic aneurysm progression in Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: Direct experiments in Marfan mouse models show protective LOX-mediated matrix maturation and demonstrate that losartan prevents LOX-inhibitor-induced aortic dilation.

unread.title: Recent Clinical Drug Trials Evidence in Marfan Syndrome and Clinical Implications.
unread.why: Clinical-trial evidence supports atenolol and losartan for reducing aortic root dilation and provides individualized treatment and monitoring recommendations for Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Differences in Arterial Events in Vascular Ehlers-Danlos, Loeys-Dietz, and Marfan Syndrome.
unread.why: A large consortium cohort provides Marfan-specific arterial-event rates and supports gene- and sex-informed surveillance and cardiovascular risk counseling.

unread.title: The role of beta-arrestin2-dependent signaling in thoracic aortic aneurysm formation in a murine model of Marfan syndrome
unread.why: Genetic deletion and siRNA experiments identify beta-arrestin2-dependent signaling as a manipulable target that delays aortic disease in a Marfan mouse model.

unread.title: Sildenafil Prevents Marfan-Associated Emphysema and Early Pulmonary Artery Dilation in Mice.
unread.why: Sildenafil treatment prevented emphysema-like alveolar destruction and delayed pulmonary artery dilation in a Marfan mouse model, with supporting lung-function and molecular data.

unread.title: Soluble EMMPRIN levels discriminate aortic ectasia in Marfan syndrome patients
unread.why: Patient plasma data show that soluble EMMPRIN can discriminate Marfan-associated aortic ectasia with reported sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and odds ratio.

unread.title: Effects of resveratrol on aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome: a single-arm open-label multicentre trial
unread.why: A multicentre clinical trial directly tested resveratrol in adults with Marfan syndrome and measured aortic expansion longitudinally by cardiac MRI.

unread.title: Functional validation reveals the novel missense V419L variant in TGFBR2 associated with Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) impairs canonical TGF-β signaling.
unread.why: The study provides an experimentally validated workflow for resolving a TGFBR2 variant of uncertain significance in a Marfan-spectrum patient with Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

unread.title: Health-related quality of life in children and adolescents with Marfan syndrome or related disorders: a controlled cross-sectional study
unread.why: A controlled pediatric Marfan study validates PedsQL and aerobic-capacity measures and relates them to disease severity and physical health.

unread.title: Losartan in combination with propranolol slows the aortic root dilatation in neonatal Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: A neonatal Marfan case reports clinical improvement and reduced aortic-root dilatation after losartan-propranolol combination treatment.

unread.title: Investigation of Strategies to Block Downstream Effectors of AT1R-Mediated Signalling to Prevent Aneurysm Formation in Marfan Syndrome.
unread.why: Direct experiments in a Marfan mouse model compared losartan with AT1R, beta-arrestin, and CCR2-directed strategies for preventing aortic aneurysm progression.

unread.title: Increased upper airway collapsibility in a mouse model of Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The paper characterizes a Marfan mouse model and an in vivo pressure assay for upper-airway collapsibility associated with obstructive sleep apnea.

unread.title: The usefulness of the genetic panel in the classification and refinement of diagnostic accuracy of Mexican patients with Marfan syndrome and other connective tissue disorders
unread.why: The study demonstrates a multigene NGS panel and annotation workflow for identifying and refining diagnoses in 136 patients with Marfan syndrome and related connective-tissue disorders.

unread.title: Application of Whole Exome Sequencing and Functional Annotations to Identify Genetic Variants Associated with Marfan Syndrome.
unread.why: The study applies whole-exome sequencing and functional annotations to identify pathogenic and candidate variants in a Marfan syndrome cohort, including novel family variants.

unread.title: Successful Mitral Valve Replacement in an Infant with Neonatal Marfan Syndrome due to a Novel Missense Mutation of the FBN1 Gene.
unread.why: A neonatal Marfan case with progressive valve regurgitation improved after early mitral valve replacement, providing direct evidence for a potentially reusable intervention.

unread.title: Growth Rate Assessed by Vascular Deformation Mapping Predicts Type B Aortic Dissection in Marfan Syndrome
unread.why: In 105 patients with Marfan syndrome, vascular deformation mapping and longitudinal CTA growth measurements predicted type B aortic dissection, including at small aortic diameters.

unread.title: Research Progress on Aortic Root Aneurysms
unread.why: Although a review, it consolidates multiple pharmacologic, surgical, and endovascular treatments for aortic-root aneurysms, a major Marfan-related complication.

unread.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations, Treatment, and Prognosis of Children With Early-Onset (Neonatal) Marfan Syndrome
unread.why: A cohort of 41 patients with early-onset Marfan syndrome identifies cardiovascular surgery as an outcome-associated intervention and provides genotype-based prognostic stratification.

unread.title: A novel variant in fibrillin-1 is responsible for early-onset familial thoracic aortic aneurysms in Marfan patients
unread.why: The study demonstrates targeted FBN1 sequencing and functional variant analysis as a diagnostic approach for identifying a pathogenic truncating variant associated with early-onset familial thoracic aortic aneurysm in Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Genotype and clinical phenotype of children with Marfan syndrome in Southeastern Anatolia
unread.why: The study validates combined clinical and FBN1 genetic assessment in 131 children and identifies genotype and longitudinal phenotypic features that can support diagnosis and monitoring of Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Growth Rate Assessed by Vascular Deformation Mapping predicts Type B Aortic Dissection in Marfan Syndrome
unread.why: This study validates vascular deformation mapping of serial CT angiography and descending-aortic growth rates as predictors of type B dissection in Marfan syndrome, including events occurring below conventional aneurysm-diameter thresholds.

unread.title: Bentall Procedure in a Marfan Syndrome Patient With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report
unread.why: The case report provides direct clinical evidence for use of Bentall surgery to manage severe aortic root dilation with markedly reduced ejection fraction in Marfan syndrome.

unread.title: Postoperative pneumothorax occurrence in patients with Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The study reports long-term outcomes of bullectomy and pulmorrhaphy for Marfan-associated pneumothorax and identifies chest deformity as a predictor of postoperative recurrence.

unread.title: Case Report: <i>FBN1</i> mutation screening in South African patients with Marfan syndrome.
unread.why: The study demonstrates targeted NGS-based FBN1 screening in a South African Marfan cohort and identifies seven pathogenic variants in eleven patients.

unread.title: Marfan Europe Network: Together we can!
unread.why: The paper describes an existing Europe-wide umbrella resource connecting fourteen national Marfan patient organizations to support education, networking, and patient engagement.
